title: Pooling with nn.MaxPool2d and nn.AvgPool2d
learning_objectives: Apply max and average pooling to (batch, channels, height, width) tensors
Compute pooled output sizes from kernel, stride and padding
Explain where max pooling sends its gradient
entry_point: pool(x, kind, kernel_size, stride=None, padding=0); pooled_size(n, kernel_size, stride=None, padding=0)
hints: Choose the class with a dict: `{"max": nn.MaxPool2d, "avg": nn.AvgPool2d}`.
`layer = cls(kernel_size, stride=stride, padding=padding)`; stride=None means stride = kernel size.
`(n + 2 * padding - kernel_size) // stride + 1` after `stride = stride or kernel_size`.

failure_feedback.advice: The output size is (n + 2p - k) // s + 1 with s defaulting to k.
Reject unknown kinds and tensors that are not 4-D.
